name: CLP Future Conservationist Award

funder.name: Conservation Leadership Programme (BirdLife International, Fauna & Flora, Wildlife Conservation Society)

summary: Annual project grants for teams of at least three early-career conservationists, nationals of an eligible low- or middle-income country, to combine research and conservation action on at-risk species and habitats.

geography.label: Low- and middle-income countries in Africa, Asia, the Pacific, Latin America and the Caribbean, Eastern and South-eastern Europe and the Middle East

eligibility.rule: Have at least three people on the project team
Have no more than five years of paid conservation experience
Have all team members be nationals, unless one non-national is clearly justified
Have no team member employed or contracted by a CLP partner
No team member is currently enrolled in a PhD programme
Last between six and twelve months
Go beyond academic research for any team member's degree
Be a new project, not a continuation of an ongoing project

status.quote: Concept notes must be submitted by the deadline of Friday, October 30, 2026, 23:59 GMT.

deadline.quote: Concept notes must be submitted by the deadline of Friday, October 30, 2026, 23:59 GMT.

applicant_types.quote: CLP supports teams of individuals with less than five years of paid conservation experience, who display a strong commitment to conservation and demonstrate leadership potential.

geography.quote: The project must take place in one of the eligible low- and middle-income countries in Africa, Asia, the Pacific, Latin America and the Caribbean, Eastern and South-eastern Europe and the Middle East.

access.quote: Concept notes should be submitted to clp.applications@birdlife.org.

window.quote: Each year, CLP calls for applications to support projects in biodiverse yet under resourced countries worldwide.

amount.quote: The total funding request from CLP must not exceed US$15,000 and CLP funding must cover at least 50% of the project budget.

effort.quote: All project teams are required to submit a completed concept note using the downloadable template from our website by the deadline 23:59 GMT Friday October 30th, 2026.
Shortlisted concept note applicants will be notified and invited to submit a full application via our online application portal.

eligibility.quote: CLP Awards are for team-based conservation projects - each team must have at least three people.

All team members must be early-career conservationists. CLP defines early-career conservationists as professionals in early stages of leading independent conservation work, with no more than five years of paid conservation experience, regardless of their age.

All team members must be nationals of the country where the project is taking place. In special cases, one team member can be a non-national subject to clear justification of the expertise brought to the team and should be a national of an eligible country.

No team member can be a part- or full-time paid employee or contractor with a CLP partner organisation, including BirdLife International, Fauna & Flora and the Wildlife Conservation Society, at any time from project development through to implementation.
Please note that undergraduate or master’s students are welcome to apply but applicants currently enrolled in a PhD programme, are not eligible to apply.
Project duration must be between six and 12 months.
Applicants must demonstrate that the proposed project goes beyond academic research being carried out for any team member's degree.
The project must be new than a continuation of an ongoing, established project.
